description: Strange Loop talks from Strange Loop 2022.

talks.title: "Expert Software Developers' Approach to Error" by Marian Petre (Strange Loop 2022)
talks.teaser: Presents expert Software Developers Approach to Error by Marian Petre (Strange Loop 2022) and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Marian Petre presents at Strange Loop 2022 on how expert software developers treat errors as opportunities rather than nuisances to be quickly swatted away.

Key Topics: Contrasting novice bug-fixing with expert approaches; errors as signals of deeper design flaws; recognizing bug clusters indicating systemic issues; and building cultures that embrace investigative debugging.

Technical Details: Petre describes how experts pause at anomalies, asking why rather than immediately patching. They examine dependencies and code structure to determine whether a bug indicates architectural misconceptions.

Takeaways: Expert developers use errors as learning inputs. Teams should cultivate curiosity about anomalies and resist pressure to ship quick fixes that mask underlying design problems.

talks.title: "Leveraging AI for Global Health" by África Periañez (Strange Loop 2022)
talks.teaser: Presents leveraging AI for Global Health by África Periañez (Strange Loop 2022) and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Global Health Context

África Periañez presents Bonsai, a Gates Foundation-funded organization bringing AI and machine learning to underserved communities. She cites stark health disparities—few doctors per capita in low-income countries and high preventable maternal mortality.

Behavioral Change Mission

Bonsai focuses on patient and provider engagement rather than raw prediction. Medication only helps if people take it and supplies exist locally, so the organization nudges behaviors toward better health outcomes using digital data.

Team Origins and Naming

Leadership backgrounds come from video-game machine learning that modeled individual player engagement. The name references Japanese benshi narrators who explained silent films—Bonsai aims to reveal what is hidden in health data.

Technical Platform

The platform organizes mobile-generated health data in low-connectivity regions, runs randomized trials and reinforcement-learning bandits, and builds recommendation, censoring, and forecasting models aimed at actionable interventions rather than prediction alone.

talks.title: "Stop Writing Dead Programs" by Jack Rusher (Strange Loop 2022)
talks.teaser: Provides stop Writing Dead Programs by Jack Rusher (Strange Loop 2022) and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Thesis

Jack Rusher's Strange Loop talk Stop Writing Dead Programs revives Seymour Papert's critique that computing education—and much of industry—still perpetuates irrational, historically inherited practices.

Punch-card era

Rusher recounts Fortran on punch cards, VAX batch jobs, 45-minute feedback loops, and terminal fear of dropped decks—hard in dumb ways unrelated to the actual problem, rewarding a priesthood with strong working memory.

Modern parallels

Today's long compile cycles, Docker/CI deploy waits, and cloud batch pipelines echo the same slow feedback; Docker exists partly because underlying stacks are overly complex.

Wrong mental model

Compile-run separation, linear single-threaded execution, and input-output-transformer programs poorly fit long-lived servers (1000-day uptimes) and rich GUI/event-driven systems we actually build.

Call to action

Mastering pointlessly hard workflows breeds pride in preserving them; Rusher urges abandoning dead program thinking for interactive, pragmatic development environments.

talks.title: "Programmable Ink" by Szymon Kaliski (Strange Loop 2022)
talks.teaser: Discusses programmable Ink by Szymon Kaliski (Strange Loop 2022) and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Dynamic Medium, Static Tools

Szymon Kaliski of Ink & Switch presents "Programmable Ink" at Strange Loop, questioning why digital drawing tools simulate paper instead of exploiting computation. Even sophisticated paint programs remain static regarding behavior—you cannot sketch seating charts that reorder when guests RSVP or bookshelves that parametrize after drawing.

## Tyranny of Formalisms

Professional design software demands pixel perfection early, pulling creators into rigid workflows. Kaliski argues the dynamic medium should blend sketching freedom with programmable behavior, avoiding premature commitment to final layouts.

## Spatial Queries Prototype

Demonstrations introduce spatial queries: canvas regions that ask which objects overlap them, returning live lists bound to UI properties. Drawing a checkbox near queried zones toggles state bidirectionally—mark removal clears lists; new marks repopulate them. Lists convert to Boolean conditions driving other elements.

## Research Toward Programmable Sketching

Programmable Ink prototypes explore how informal diagrams gain reactive logic without traditional coding. The research track targets creators who think visually first, enabling iterative exploration where hand-drawn structures carry executable semantics—a middle ground between whiteboards and production CAD systems.
